bull.b: Affirm has moved from substantial losses to meaningful profitability while generating significant operating and free cash flow. This improves internal funding capacity, supports investment in products and distribution, and provides a stronger foundation for absorbing normal credit or funding volatility over the next several quarters.

A materially stronger underwriting architecture can improve approval rates without increasing expected losses, supporting both transaction growth and customer reach. If performance persists, the capability may strengthen Affirm’s economics and create a durable advantage in point-of-sale lending.

Low current penetration and geographic coverage leave substantial room for expansion without relying solely on higher usage from existing customers. Broader merchant, market, and distribution adoption could support sustained volume growth and improve operating leverage as the platform scales.

bear.b: The latest balance sheet is relatively lightly leveraged, but the sharp historical swings show that funding needs and capital structure can change materially. That variability may reduce financial flexibility during weaker credit conditions and makes current earnings and balance-sheet strength less certain.

Higher provisions, modestly worsening delinquencies, and rising funding costs can compress lending economics even when transaction volumes grow. These pressures directly affect credit losses and financing expense, creating an ongoing risk to the sustainability of current margins and cash generation.

A greater contribution from card-based direct-to-consumer activity can dilute revenue earned per unit of GMV because interchange is lower than integrated-merchant fees. If this mix persists, Affirm may need stronger volume growth or operating efficiency to maintain revenue and margin expansion.
